Residents burst firecrackers while wearing face masks during the ‘Deepavali’ festival celebrations, near Akshardham Temple in New Delhi. File | Photo Credit: PTI
More than 200 cases were registered across Delhi districts for violations of prescribed firecracker timings during Deepavali celebrations, officials said on Monday. Meanwhile, the Delhi Fire Service (DFS) received 257 calls on the festival day, including two massive (Make-4 category) fires and one medium-category incident. The number of calls was 12 fewer than the 269 reported last year.
Chief Fire Officer Abhilash Malik said firefighting operations were handled more proactively this year, with personnel deployed across 71 fire stations to ensure wider coverage of the city.
“We had identified key target areas and deployed our quick response teams to tackle any emergency situations,” he said.
Fire calls peaked during the night and early hours of Monday, with the department responding to 281 calls between 6 p.m. on November 8 and 6 a.m. on November 9. “The number is high, but we were able to manage efficiently,” Mr. Malik said.
Ahead of Deepavali, the DFS had strengthened its emergency response arrangements by deploying additional firefighting personnel and vehicles at vulnerable locations, including congested residential areas and crowded markets. Quick Response Teams were stationed at identified hotspots to ensure a prompt response. The department also kept its control room and emergency response network on high alert.
Of the 257 calls, 214 were fire-related, including 24 concerning firecrackers. The remaining calls involved animal and bird rescues, house collapses, human rescues and other incidents, according to official data. The department also received a call from Sonepat, following which three fire tenders were sent to the area.
Five fire personnel were injured during firefighting operations. Station Officer (STO) Naveen Thakran sustained burns to his hand while responding to a fire in Nangli Sakrawati in southwest Delhi. He was advised seven days of medical rest. Another officer, Sita Ram, fractured his hand while attending to a fire at a godown in Libaspur in northwest Delhi.
